art.prompt: Late afternoon in the dusty earth yard of a small West African village school, a low building with a long veranda and a big shade tree behind. On the right third of the frame a small boy of about seven in a yellow shirt stands with his hands pressed together in prayer, his mouth closed, his eyes cast down, shy and a little sad. A kind man in a plain blue t-shirt kneels on one knee in front of him so his face is at the boy's eye level, seen in profile, one hand resting gently on the boy's shoulder, smiling softly. Far behind them, small and out of focus, two other children stand with folded hands. Warm low golden sunlight falls through the leaves of the tree and rims the boy's face and shoulders. Large calm empty area of soft golden haze and tree shade on the left.

Early morning on a quiet grassy hillside above a calm lake. In the centre, seen directly from behind, a man in a simple cream robe kneels on the grass in prayer with a brown cloth draped over his head and shoulders like a hood, his head slightly bowed and turned fully away from us toward the sunrise, so that no part of his face, cheek or profile can be seen, only the back of the head-cloth and his shoulders. A little to the left of him, three men in simple robes of brown, blue and grey kneel on the grass too, heads bowed, hands folded, learning the prayer from him; their faces are turned down and in soft shadow. The first golden light of sunrise spills over the hill from the right and rims their shoulders. Large calm empty area of pale gold morning sky across the top.

Night inside a small one-room home with deep teal walls. On the right third of the frame a West African father in a green patterned shirt kneels on a woven mat beside his small son of about seven in a yellow shirt; both have their hands folded. The boy prays with his eyes closed and his face lifted; the father kneels lower beside him with his head bowed and eyes closed, listening to his son pray like a child himself. A single candle burns on a low wooden table beside them. Soft golden light falls on both of them from a small high window. Large calm empty area of teal wall on the left.

titles: Learning To Say “Our Father” | Day 4 · The Father Showed Up
When “Father” Is A Hard Word To Say
The Word “Father” Still Belongs To God
social.description:
For some children “Father” is a hard word, because of a man who left or one they have never met. Tonight we learn that the word still belongs to God, who sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts so we can cry, “Abba, Father.”

THE WORD: Galatians 4:6 (read Galatians 4:4–7 aloud)
TONIGHT, children: say “Our Father” slowly and quietly, three times. If it is hard tonight, just listen while others say it.
TONIGHT, fathers: say the two words out loud, once, slowly. Then pray the whole prayer. If you cannot finish, start with the first two words.
SAY IT: God is my Father. I am His child.
